packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-11 -- unverified blind image reading (UTF-8 plain text)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification
or reading of this packet. I did not open packet.json. Beyond the rules I only
measured image pixel sizes (sips) and made crops of packet tiles.

LAYOUT SURVEY

Face 1 (overview image-001.jpg; tiles image-002..005, horizontal strips top to
bottom, overlapping):
- Paper/parchment fragment cut to an irregular elongated octagon; ruler at foot
  (approx. 15 cm shown). Upright orientation.
- One main text column survives nearly whole (about 44-45 lines), written in a
  small, heavily abbreviated Gothic cursive/bastarda-like hand, brown ink.
- A vertical fold/crease runs down the middle of the column with holes and
  losses along it (worst in the middle and lower half); the lower centre is cut
  away as a deep slot.
- Red paragraph marks (pilcrows) visible: line ~6 right side ("¶ Et"),
  ~line 18 left ("¶ Circa"), ~line 30 right ("¶ Videtur"?).
- At the far right edge, initial letters/fragments of a second column (the
  neighbouring column, cut away) are visible: line-beginnings only.
- At left margin near line 3-4 a faint marginal word ("...cond(i)c(i)o"?).
- A small stamp at lower left margin (library stamp, not read).
- Content tentatively looks like legal prose (repeated "condictio", "ff." and
  "C." allegations, "l." = lex). Observation only; no identification.

TRANSCRIPTION

Conventions: (x) = proposed expansion; word? = uncertain; [illegible]; [hole]
= physical loss on the leaf. Line numbers are counted from the top of each
tile image. Each tile was viewed as a crop of that tile (left margin of the
tile trimmed; crop file noted). Main column only unless marked "right-edge".

- One main column, more densely written than face 1 (about 55-58 lines), same

- Left edge: line-ends of the neighbouring column (cut), with several words
  per line visible near the top (e.g. "...lle(?)").
- Central crease with holes; lower centre cut away as a slot (same slot as
  face 1).
- Red pilcrows at ~line 7 (centre), ~line 33 (centre), ~line 39 (left),
  ~line 48 (centre-left).
- A two-line-high enlarged initial-like stroke at top of column (near x 360
  and 430 overview: tall ascenders, perhaps cadels on line 1).
- Small library stamp at lower right margin (not read).
